Despite all the time that’s passed, and every law that’s been changed over the course of (Insert GUYs that have passed between campaigns), Floran slavery still thrives. It was never banned, never abolished in any way. Some planets refuse the practice, of course, but the majority of the galaxy still keeps slaves.

Nehe, a small Floran child, trains day in and day out on a tiny middle-of-nowhere planet. He’s too young to really understand what he’s training for, and some days he even enjoys the exercise. But the slave masters make sure he isn’t caught having much fun. For them, it’s all about military discipline. Nehe might not have known exactly what was going on, but he knew enough to realize he was in trouble. The compound he was located in was a military training base so secretive that not even the Galactic Union could find it.

He wasn’t the only slave there, and not even the only Floran. An old war veteran who was aged with bark, and wiser than anyone else Nehe knew, sat alone in the corner of the slaves’ quarters, watching over everyone else. He acted as the elder of the group, and Nehe’s personal mentor. It was after lights out, but Nehe carefully made his way over to the old man. After a brief silence, Nehe spoke up:

“[Can you tell the story again, what it’sss like out there?]{Nehe}”

The old Floran cracked as he moved, making the bark around his face and joints crunch under his motions. “[Out where, small one?]{Old Floran}” He had no hiss like Nehe, which was more common in young Florans who didn’t quite have a full grasp on language yet.

“[Where floran can sssee the ssstars. Masssters are mean, don’t want to be here…]{Nehe}”

“[Well, young man, it’s a fantastic sight. An endless night, but not like the ones back home. It’s a boundless sea of stars that stretches to infinity. Infinite planets, infinite places to explore.]{Old Floran}” As the old man recounted his tales of the space beyond the slaves’ compound, other slaves started to wake up. Some groaned groggily, but everyone was listening intently. “[I used to sit in my captain’s chair and wonder where I wanted to go next. Perhaps I would try an ice planet, or an ocean planet. There’s only so much jungle you can see before it starts to make you feel homesick…]{Old Floran}”

It was a story everyone had heard before, but no one ever got tired of it; it gave them hope. But this time, at the end of the story, he leaned forward and looked Nehe right in his eyes. “[Someday, I wish to take you out there, Nehe. Everyone in this room deserves to see the cosmos, and I want you to be their captain. You may not be the oldest or most experienced, but there’s something special in you. Can you feel the calling?]{Old Floran}”

Nehe put his hand up to his heart. He was desperate to get out of there, he knew that much; anything would be better than working for those jerks. He moved his hand from his heart to his head in a respectful salute. “[Floran would do anything for that chanccce!]{Nehe}”

The old man’s oaken face split into a proud grin. “[Then take this, captain, and lead your own adventure. See the galaxy for all its beauty.]{Old Floran}” He reached into a knot in his bark and pulled out a badge. The badge was a brilliant blue and purple star, with the words “CPTN of the INTERSTELLAR DREAM.”

Nehe was speechless. He held the badge up high, and a single ray of light from a crack in the slaves’ quarters’ door shone onto it, making it glimmer for all to see. He brought it back down, hugged the old Floran, and tucked in for bed.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The next morning, everyone was called into the courtroom for a meeting. The slave master looked furious.

“[ALRIGHT, EVERYONE, LINE UP! It has come to our attention that one of you HAS BEEN TRYING TO ESCAPE!]{Slave Master}” He pointed to a hole in the floor in the far corner of the room, which had a rug lying next to it, as if the hole had been concealed by it. “[IF ONE OF YOU MAGGOTS DOESN’T SPEAK UP, EVERYONE GETS PUNISHED!]{Slave Master}”

Nobody said a word.

“[Alright then. Eeny, meeny, miney, YOU.]{Slave Master}” He grabbed Nehe by the wrist and yanked him off the ground. “[You’ve got till the count of three to speak up. One…Two…]{Slave Master}”

“[It was me.]{Old Floran}”

Everyone turned to see the old Floran stepping forward. He was looking straight forward, was standing board-straight, and had not one tear in his eye. A fearless captain, to the very last moment.

The slave master dropped Nehe. “[See, was that really so hard? Now, STEP. FORTH.]{Slave Master}” The old man obliged, still with those fearless eyes. “[I’m a fair man. If you REALLY want to escape, I’ll give you a chance. Defeat me in single combat, and you’ll get to go free.]{Slave Master}”

The old Floran, despite his background, was far too elderly to be of much use in combat anymore. Nonetheless, he stanced up for what he knew would be his last fistfight. Unfortunately, the slave master was not looking for fair fisticuffs. At the Floran’s first approach, he sidestepped the lunge and pulled a knife to slice the back of his slave.

The old man yelled in agony, but straightened his spine and faced his master. He went for another punch before being met with the same cutting blow.

Nehe could barely stand to watch. He knew the slave master would kill him if he stepped out of line, but his mentor was going to die if he didn’t do anything. And wasn’t it the old man who stepped up to take the blame for the hole, so that Nehe wouldn’t be hurt? He had to do something. As the old Floran was sliced more and more, Nehe grew angrier. Thoughts clouded his mind. Who were these guys to treat all of them like this? With so many more slaves than guards, why had nobody stepped up before? And most of all:

He would not allow these people to rob him of seeing the stars.

Nehe lunged forward with sudden ferocity, his claws and teeth bared in a terrifying display of Floran wrath. He landed onto the slave master and tore at his arms, legs, or any skin he could find. The slave master ROARED in pain, but Nehe was too blinded by rage. After recovering for a few seconds, the old Floran shouted, “[RUN, Nehe! We’ll hold them back, just get OUT OF HERE!]{Old Floran}”

The elder’s voice brought Nehe back to the present. He wiped the blood off his lips and ran for the hole at the far corner of the room. Before jumping in, he looked back to see every slave fighting for his freedom. What made them all want to do this just for him? He didn’t have time to worry about it. His mentor shared one final salute with the boy before Nehe slipped and fell in.

He quickly stood up and ran for the other side of the tunnel. It wasn’t a long one, just big enough to get on the other side of the wall of the complex. Nehe crawled out the other side and gawked at the sky. A boundless sea of stars met his eye, and he was almost unable to look away. Eventually, he gathered himself enough to look at his surroundings. He was in an alley between two parts of the complex, and at the end of it was a fleet of ships arranged in perfect order. None of the guards had seen him yet, nor heard the commotion from inside through the thick walls. Nehe, a master of blending in due to his plant-like body, did his best to sneak towards one of the ships. Miraculously, no one noticed him. Silent as the night, he scrambled his way into the cockpit of one of the personal space jets.

Suddenly, he realized he had no idea how to fly a spaceship. He was about to start mashing buttons when he heard a voice coming from the console: “[Hello, I am your autopilot. Please select your destination.]{Autopilot}”

Nehe said in his quietest voice, “[Take floran sssomewhere sssafe!]{Nehe}”

“[Set course for: ‘Somewhere.’ Forest planet in quadrant C. We will arrive in…94 minutes. Prepare for hyperspeed.]{Autopilot}”

Nehe strapped himself in and looked out the window to see dozens of guards shouting at each other and pointing at the ship. Some aimed their guns, which made Nehe sit a little lower in his seat. Blaster rounds pinged off the ship as it lifted into the sky, but in the blink of an eye, it entered hyperspeed and left for a planet named “Somewhere.”
